_help: This is the ONE file that controls detection. Edit it and save - the monitor reloads it live, no restart needed.
Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions written as JSON strings, so a backslash is doubled: \d means a digit.
(?<id>...) captures the object ID. Rules are tried top to bottom; the first match wins.
Run ./inspect.sh on the CTF VM to learn the real cookie names, endpoints and ID formats, then adjust below.

identity._help: How to work out WHICH STUDENT sent a request. Tried in this order: JWT, session cookie (learned at login), X-Forwarded-For / IP.

login._help: When a login succeeds, remember 'this session cookie = this username'. The password is never stored.

whoami._help: Endpoints that return the current user. Used to learn the student's name and their own user ID.

_help: The IDOR targets. Each entry: name, (optional) methods, pattern, idFrom, owner.
owner:   'auto' (default) = ownership.json, then 'it is their own user id', then learn from first quiet success
'same-as-user' = the object ID must equal the student's own user ID (profile pages)
'learn'        = the first student to quietly read it owns it
'none'         = only track the IDs (enumeration), no ownership check

ownership._help: Optional fixed map of who owns what: config/ownership.json. Set learnFromFirstSuccess=false to only trust that file + same-as-user.

enumeration._help: N different IDs on the same endpoint within W seconds

bruteForce._help: N responses with one of these statuses within W seconds

successMinBytes._help: A 2xx with at least this many body bytes counts as 'contains data'

masking._help: Any field or URL parameter whose name CONTAINS one of these words is replaced by *** in logs and on the dashboard.

ignore._help: Requests matching these are forwarded normally but NOT shown or logged (static files, health checks).
